d: Karnataka government claims petrol sold in the state contains up to 31.2 percent ethanol, far exceeding the central government’s E20 standard of 20 percent blending. Samples collected from pumps of HPCL, BPCL, Nayara Energy, Shell and Indian Oil across seven districts showed ethanol levels ranging from 25.5 to 31.2 percent, raising concerns over reduced mileage, engine damage, fuel system corrosion and higher maintenance costs for vehicle owners.
